md_description: This workflow models the generation and analysis of single-cell amplified genomes from uncultured marine microbes. Individual marine microbial cells are isolated by microfluidics, lysed, and subjected to multiple displacement amplification before sequencing. The resulting sequence data are assembled and annotated with bioinformatics software to reconstruct draft genomes and compute assembly quality metrics for downstream ecological and diversity analyses.

marine_microbial_cell.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the study object itself: the uncultured marine microbial cell’s intrinsic identity and origin. I included fields for sample/cell identity and environmental provenance because those belong to the object, not to the isolation or downstream processing steps. I excluded isolation device settings, lysis conditions, amplification parameters, sequencing, software, and quality metrics because those are owned by downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating any likely root-level identifiers by keeping the schema focused on biological source context and basic intrinsic descriptors rather than experiment-wide IDs.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the individual marine microbial cell used as the study object; use a stable string format such as SAG_cell_001. Record once at the entity level before isolation or processing.

Best available taxonomic identification of the uncultured cell at the time of study, reported as a string (for example, phylum/class/genus if known). Record from upstream sample knowledge or preliminary classification, not from downstream genome annotation.

Source environment of the cell, describing the marine habitat from which it originated; examples include surface seawater, deep seawater, coastal water, or marine sediment porewater. Record as the origin of the entity, not the collection method.
Name or label of the marine sampling location where the original environmental sample containing the cell was obtained; use a string such as station name, cruise station, or transect label.
Latitude of the original environmental sampling location in decimal degrees (range -90 to 90). Record the geographic origin of the entity, not the isolation device position.
Longitude of the original environmental sampling location in decimal degrees (range -180 to 180). Record the geographic origin of the entity, not the isolation device position.

Water column or sediment depth at which the source sample was collected, in meters (typical marine range 0 to several thousand meters). Record this as provenance of the cell’s originating environment.
Date when the original environmental sample containing this cell was collected, in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. This documents the provenance time point for the entity.

Estimated diameter or characteristic cell size in micrometers, if known from prior imaging or cell sorting context. Report the intrinsic physical size of the entity rather than capture settings; typical microbial cell sizes are about 0.1 to 10 micrometers.

Observed cell shape or morphology when known from microscopy prior to isolation; examples include coccoid, rod-shaped, spiral, filamentous, or pleomorphic. Record as an intrinsic descriptive property of the cell.

microfluidic_isolation.reasoning: This Process node should describe how a single cell was isolated using the microfluidic setup. I included operational parameters that define the isolation method and its execution, plus the microfluidic instrument details required to reproduce the step. I excluded cell identity/origin fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded downstream outputs such as the isolated cell’s properties because those belong to the output Entity node. I also avoided overlap with later lysis, amplification, sequencing, or software nodes, and did not repeat any already_generated entity-level fields.

md_schema.descr: Primary cell isolation method used in the microfluidic step; for this workflow it should describe the microfluidic partitioning approach used to isolate a single marine microbial cell. Record the method actually applied at the moment of isolation.
Manufacturer or vendor of the microfluidic instrument used for single-cell isolation. Record the hardware maker responsible for the instrument performing the isolation.
Model name or number of the microfluidic device used for cell isolation; use the exact instrument model string as reported by the manufacturer.
Serial number or other unique hardware identifier for the microfluidic device used in the isolation step, if available. Record the instrument identifier for traceability of the capture operation.

Composition of the fluid used during microfluidic isolation, including key salts, media, or surfactants if relevant to maintaining cell integrity during capture. Record the operational buffer used at the time of isolation, not the source environment.

Characteristic microfluidic channel or trap dimensions in micrometers that were configured for isolating individual cells; report the relevant feature size(s) used during the capture session, typically in the range of a few to hundreds of micrometers.

Percentage of attempted isolation events that resulted in recovery of a single cell during the microfluidic session. Record as an operational performance indicator for the isolation process, typically between 0 and 100.
How the operator confirmed that a single cell was isolated after microfluidic capture; examples include microscopic inspection, fluorescence check, or image-based verification.

isolated_single_cell.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the recovered single-cell specimen after isolation, focusing on its state and identity as the isolated object. I included fields capturing whether the cell was recovered intact, how many cells were present in the isolate, and any immediate handling state that characterizes the entity after microfluidic partitioning. I excluded isolation hardware settings and method details because those belong to the microfluidic_isolation Process node, and I excluded lysis, amplification, and sequencing details because they are downstream processes. I also avoided repeating the original cell provenance and taxonomic fields already assigned to the upstream marine_microbial_cell entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier assigned to the isolated single-cell specimen after microfluidic partitioning; use a stable string format such as ISC_001. This identifies the recovered entity, not the original environmental cell record.

Number of cells physically present in the isolated specimen after partitioning; expected value is 1 for a successful single-cell isolate, but record the observed count if estimated by microscopy or imaging at the time of recovery.

Assessment of the physical condition of the isolated cell immediately after recovery, indicating whether it appeared intact or damaged during handling. Record the entity state at the post-isolation point.

Immediate storage or holding condition of the isolated cell before lysis, such as temperature or buffer state, recorded as a brief string (for example, 4 C in buffer, on ice, or in recovery medium). This describes the entity’s handling state after isolation.

Short note describing how the isolated cell was verified as a single recovered specimen, if applicable; for example, microscopy-confirmed or image-verified. This is a descriptive property of the recovered entity rather than the isolation process setup.

cell_lysis.reasoning: This Process node should describe how the isolated single cell was lysed to release genomic DNA. I included lysis method, reagents, and the key operational conditions that determine the transformation, plus a simple success indicator because it is part of process execution quality. I excluded cell identity and isolate-state fields because they belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded released DNA properties because those belong to the downstream lysed_cell_material Entity. I also avoided any amplification, sequencing, or assembly terms, and did not repeat already_generated entity-level identifiers or isolation details.

md_schema.descr: Method used to lyse the isolated single cell and release genomic DNA; for example, chemical lysis, thermal lysis, enzymatic lysis, freeze-thaw, or combined protocols. Record the method applied at the moment of lysis.
Primary lysis reagent or reagent mixture used during the cell_lysis step, such as proteinase K, alkali, detergent, or buffer name. Record the reagent actually applied to the isolated cell.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used during the lysis step, measured during the lysis reaction or incubation. Typical ranges for single-cell lysis are about 4 to 95 degrees Celsius depending on protocol.
Duration of the lysis incubation or treatment in minutes, measured from the start of the lysis step to completion. Typical values range from a few minutes to several hours depending on the protocol.
Composition of the buffer or reaction mixture used for lysis, including key salts, detergents, enzymes, and pH if known. Record the operational lysis environment used for releasing genomic DNA.
Whether the lysis step successfully released material suitable for downstream genome amplification, based on operator observation or immediate assay. Record as a process outcome indicator.
Name of the lysis protocol or operating procedure used for this step, if a named protocol was followed; for example, a lab SOP or published protocol identifier.

lysed_cell_material.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the material state produced by lysis: the lysed-cell extract containing released genomic DNA. I included fields that characterize the material’s composition, volume, and storage state because those are intrinsic properties of the post-lysis entity. I excluded the lysis method, reagents, temperature, and duration because those belong to the upstream cell_lysis Process node, and I excluded amplification parameters because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating isolation or original cell provenance fields already assigned to earlier entity nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the lysed cell material derived from the isolated single cell; use a stable string format such as LCM_001. This identifies the post-lysis entity and should not be reused for the original cell or downstream DNA products.
Whether visible cellular debris remained after lysis, as observed immediately after the lysis step. Record as a property of the material state, not as a process outcome.
Whether genomic DNA was visibly or assay-detected in the lysed material at the time of transfer to amplification. This describes the post-lysis material content prior to downstream processing.
Approximate volume of the lysed-cell material handled after lysis, in microliters. Typical single-cell lysis reaction volumes are often in the sub-microliter to tens of microliters range.

Name of the buffer or medium in which the lysed material was held before amplification, if applicable; for example, lysis buffer, TE buffer, or water. Record the material’s immediate storage environment.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the lysed material was held before downstream amplification, measured during the post-lysis holding period. Typical values include 4, -20, or -80 degrees Celsius depending on workflow.
Time in hours between lysis completion and transfer of the lysed material to the amplification step, if known. Record the holding interval for the entity before downstream processing.

mda_amplification.reasoning: This Process node should describe how the released genomic DNA was amplified by multiple displacement amplification (MDA). I included the amplification chemistry, polymerase/reagent details, and core reaction conditions that control the process, along with a simple process success indicator. I also included software/reagent-style agent detail only insofar as it belongs to the process execution, but not instrument hardware because this is a bench reaction rather than a Capture node. I excluded upstream lysis/material properties and downstream amplified DNA properties because those belong to the input Entity and output Entity respectively, and I avoided duplicating any already_generated fields such as lysis-related metadata or isolate identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Genome amplification method used for this step; for this workflow it should specify multiple displacement amplification of released genomic DNA. Record the method applied at the moment of amplification.
Name of the polymerase or kit enzyme used for MDA, such as phi29 DNA polymerase or a kit-equivalent enzyme preparation. Record the enzyme actually used in the amplification reaction.
Temperature in degrees Celsius used during the MDA reaction, measured at the amplification incubation stage. Typical MDA temperatures are around 30 degrees Celsius.
Duration of the MDA incubation in hours, measured from reaction start to termination. Typical values range from a few hours to overnight.
Total reaction volume for the MDA setup in microliters, recorded at the start of amplification. Typical single-cell MDA reaction volumes are often in the low-microliter range.
Estimated amount of input DNA in picograms entering the MDA reaction, if known or calculated from lysed material. Record the quantity of template DNA present at the amplification start.
Whether the MDA reaction yielded amplifiable genomic DNA suitable for downstream sequencing, based on operator assessment or immediate QC. Record as a process outcome indicator.
Brief notes on the MDA reaction outcome, such as high-yield, low-yield, or preferential amplification, recorded as a process summary for the amplification step.

amplified_sag_dna.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the amplified DNA preparation itself: what material exists after MDA, how much of it was obtained, and whether it is suitable for sequencing. I included yield, concentration, purity, and fragment-size characteristics because these are intrinsic properties of the amplified SAG DNA entity. I excluded MDA chemistry, temperature, and duration because those belong to the upstream mda_amplification Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the downstream Capture node. I also avoided repeating lysis or source-cell provenance fields already defined on earlier entities.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the amplified single amplified genome DNA preparation; use a stable string format such as SAGDNA_001. This identifies the post-amplification entity used for sequencing.

Total amount of amplified DNA recovered from the MDA reaction, measured in nanograms at the time of cleanup or transfer to sequencing. Typical SAG yields can span from sub-ng to many hundreds of ng depending on reaction performance.
Concentration of the amplified SAG DNA preparation in nanograms per microliter, measured after amplification and any cleanup step before sequencing library preparation.

Purity ratio of the amplified DNA preparation, typically A260/A280 or an equivalent spectrophotometric purity metric, measured after amplification and cleanup. Record the numeric ratio used to assess the entity’s quality.

Approximate dominant fragment size or size range of the amplified DNA preparation in base pairs, measured after amplification and before sequencing. Typical MDA products are often highly heterogeneous; report the representative size if assessed.
Immediate storage condition of the amplified DNA preparation before sequencing, such as 4 C, -20 C, or -80 C, recorded as a descriptive string.
Whether the amplified DNA preparation met the practical requirements for downstream sequencing library preparation. Record as an entity-level readiness flag for the DNA material.

sag_sequencing_capture.reasoning: This Capture node should describe the sequencing session and instrument configuration used to measure the amplified SAG DNA. I included instrument make/model/serial, sequencing chemistry, run layout, and actively controlled run settings because those belong to the capture operation. I excluded library properties and raw read file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node, and I excluded upstream amplified DNA yield/purity because those belong to the input Entity. I also avoided software and assembly fields because those are downstream process or derivative territory, and I did not repeat any already_generated identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the SAG sequencing capture session. Record the hardware maker responsible for the sequencing measurement.
Model name or number of the sequencing instrument used to generate raw reads from the amplified SAG DNA; use the exact instrument model string as reported by the vendor.
Serial number or unique hardware identifier for the sequencing instrument used during the capture session, if available. Record the instrument traceability identifier.

Sequencing platform or chemistry family used for the capture session, such as Illumina short-read sequencing or other supported platform types. Record the platform actually used to measure the amplified SAG DNA.
Read structure configured for the run, such as single-end or paired-end. Record the active measurement configuration used during sequencing.
Nominal read length in base pairs configured for the sequencing run, measured as the planned or reported read length for the capture session. Typical values depend on platform and chemistry.
Instrument run identifier or flow-cell/run accession assigned to this capture session, using the vendor or facility's run naming convention.
Lane identifier or flow-cell identifier used for the sequencing capture, if applicable. Record the physical partition of the run used to generate the raw reads.
Number of sequencing cycles executed during the run, if the platform reports cycle count. Record the run setting that governs measurement depth and read completion.

Basecalling or instrument control software version used during the sequencing capture session, if applicable. Record the version actively used to convert instrument signals into sequence calls at the capture stage.

raw_sag_reads.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the raw sequencing data artifact itself, not the sequencing instrument or the biological sample. I included file format, size, read counts, technical dimensions, and basic raw-data quality metrics because these characterize the data product generated by capture. I excluded sequencing run settings and instrument details because those belong to the sag_sequencing_capture Capture node, and I excluded filtering, assembly, and annotation details because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating amplified DNA properties or upstream identifiers already generated.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw read file produced by the sequencer, using the original data file naming convention; for example, sample_R1.fastq.gz or a facility-specific equivalent.
File format of the raw sequencing reads as delivered from the sequencing capture session; for example, FASTQ, BAM, or SRA-derived raw reads. Record the technical file type of the signal artifact.
Size of the raw read file in bytes at the time of storage or transfer. Record the technical storage size of the signal artifact.

Total number of raw reads contained in the sequencing file or file set, counted at the signal level after capture. Typical SAG datasets may contain from thousands to millions of reads depending on sequencing depth.
Total number of bases represented in the raw sequencing reads, in base pairs. Record the aggregate sequence content of the signal artifact.
Mean read length in base pairs calculated from the raw reads, reflecting the technical output dimensions of the file at the signal stage.
Primary raw-data quality metric reported for the file, such as mean Q score, percent bases above Q30, or equivalent technical quality statistic. Record the metric assessed on the raw signal artifact.
File path, object store URI, or accession where the raw reads are stored; for example, a local path, cloud bucket URI, or archive accession. Record the storage location of the signal artifact.
Checksum or hash for the raw read file used to verify data integrity, such as MD5 or SHA256. Record the technical integrity identifier for the signal artifact.

read_filtering.reasoning: This Process node should describe how raw SAG reads were filtered and trimmed before assembly. I included the software agent details, filtering/trimming tool parameters, thresholds, and a process-level output quality indicator because these belong to the transformation step itself. I excluded raw file properties and storage location because those belong to the upstream raw_sag_reads Signal node, and I excluded filtered read file properties because those belong to the downstream filtered_sag_reads Signal node. I also avoided assembly, annotation, and derivative metrics, and did not repeat any already_generated capture or entity identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to filter and trim the raw sequencing reads before assembly; for this workflow it should identify the read-cleaning tool actually applied.
Version of the read-filtering software used in this process step, recorded as the exact release string used during execution.
Repository, package source, or reference location for the filtering software used in this step, such as a GitHub URL, conda package name, or published release citation.
Whether adapter trimming was enabled during read filtering. Record as a process setting used at the time of cleanup.
Phred quality threshold used for trimming low-quality bases from raw reads, recorded as the numeric cutoff applied during filtering. Typical values are often between 10 and 30.
Minimum read length in base pairs retained after trimming; reads shorter than this threshold were discarded during filtering. Record the length cutoff used for cleanup.
Whether paired reads were synchronized and retained together during filtering, if paired-end data were processed. Record the handling policy applied during the cleanup step.

Percentage of raw reads retained after filtering and trimming, calculated at the end of the process. Record this as a process-level quality indicator for cleanup performance, typically between 0 and 100.
Brief summary of why reads were removed during filtering, such as adapter contamination, low quality, or short length. Record the process-level decision basis for cleanup.

filtered_sag_reads.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the cleaned read data artifact produced by filtering, not the filtering software or parameters themselves. I included file naming, format, size, retained read counts, and technical quality metrics because those characterize the processed signal artifact used for assembly. I excluded raw-read properties and capture settings because those belong upstream, and I excluded assembly and derivative quality because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating already_generated identifiers and software/process fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the filtered read file produced after read cleaning, using the retained-data naming convention; for example, sample_trimmed_R1.fastq.gz or facility-specific equivalent.
File format of the filtered SAG reads after trimming and cleanup; for example, FASTQ, BAM, or another retained-read format. Record the technical file type of the signal artifact.
Size of the filtered read file in bytes at the time of storage or transfer. Record the technical storage size of the cleaned signal artifact.

Total number of reads retained after filtering and trimming, counted at the signal level after cleanup. This value is typically lower than the raw read count and is used to track usable sequence data for assembly.
Total number of bases represented in the filtered reads, in base pairs. Record the aggregate sequence content available for assembly after cleanup.
Mean read length in base pairs calculated from the filtered reads, reflecting the technical dimensions of the cleaned data artifact.
Primary quality metric reported for the filtered reads, such as mean Q score or percent bases above Q30, measured on the cleaned signal artifact before assembly.

File path, object store URI, or accession where the filtered reads are stored; for example, a local path, cloud bucket URI, or archive accession. Record the storage location of the cleaned signal artifact.
Checksum or hash for the filtered read file used to verify data integrity, such as MD5 or SHA256. Record the technical integrity identifier for the cleaned signal artifact.

genome_assembly.reasoning: This Process node should describe how filtered SAG reads were assembled into a draft genome. I included assembly software agent details, algorithmic parameters, and process-level output metrics such as contig/scaffold counts and assembly contiguity because those belong to the transformation step. I excluded filtered read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting draft genome object itself because its properties belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided annotation and QC metrics that are handled by separate downstream processes, and did not repeat any already_generated process or capture fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the assembly software used to reconstruct contigs and scaffolds from filtered reads; for this workflow it should identify the assembler actually applied.
Version of the assembly software used in this process step, recorded as the exact release string executed for genome reconstruction.
Repository, package source, or reference location for the assembly software used in this step, such as a GitHub URL, conda package name, or published release citation.
K-mer sizes or k-mer set used by the assembler, recorded as the parameter values configured for this assembly run. Typical values are software-specific and should be listed exactly as used.

Minimum contig length in base pairs retained in the assembly output, measured as the length cutoff used during or after assembly. Typical values are often 200 to 1000 bp depending on reporting standards.
Assembly mode or strategy selected in the assembler for this run, such as careful, single-cell, meta, or default if the software supports modes. Record the operating mode used for reconstruction.
Total number of contigs produced by the assembly process before or after standard length filtering, recorded as a process-level output metric.
Total number of scaffolds produced by the assembly process, if scaffolding was performed, recorded as a process-level output metric.

N50 contig or scaffold length in base pairs computed from the assembly output, used as a process-level contiguity indicator at the end of assembly. Report the metric exactly as calculated for the draft genome reconstruction.
Total assembled sequence length in base pairs generated by the assembly step, recorded as a process-level output metric for the reconstructed draft genome.

draft_sag_genome.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed draft genome assembly itself, not the assembly software or input reads. I included fields that characterize the resulting draft genome product: assembly identifier, sequence counts, size, continuity, completeness/contamination-style summary, and storage provenance. I excluded assembly parameters because those belong to the genome_assembly Process node, and I excluded annotation and QC software outputs because those belong to downstream processes and their derivative tables. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields for the upstream reads or capture stages.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the draft SAG genome assembly product; use a stable string format such as SAGASM_001. This identifies the computed assembly derivative, not the raw reads or assembler run.
Number of contigs present in the final draft genome assembly after standard filtering, as represented by the derivative genome object.
Number of scaffolds present in the final draft genome assembly, if scaffolding was performed, as represented by the derivative genome object.
Total assembled sequence length of the draft SAG genome in base pairs, measured for the final derivative assembly product.
N50 contig or scaffold length in base pairs for the final draft genome assembly, reported as a derivative quality descriptor of genome contiguity.

Estimated completeness of the draft genome assembly as a percentage, typically derived from downstream assessment tools but recorded here as a property of the draft genome product itself. Values usually range from 0 to 100.
Estimated contamination level of the draft genome assembly as a percentage, representing non-target sequence content in the assembled derivative. Values usually range from 0 to 100.
GC content of the final draft genome assembly, expressed as a percentage of total bases that are G or C in the derivative sequence.
File path, object store URI, or archive accession where the draft genome assembly is stored; for example, a local path, cloud bucket URI, or repository accession.
Checksum or hash for the draft genome assembly file used to verify data integrity, such as MD5 or SHA256. Record the technical integrity identifier for the derivative artifact.

genome_annotation.reasoning: This Process node should describe how the draft SAG genome was annotated using software to assign genes and functional features. I included annotation software identity and version, database/source references, and key annotation settings because those belong to the transformation step. I also included process-level output indicators such as predicted gene count and feature counts because they summarize the annotation run itself. I excluded draft genome sequence properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the annotated genome product properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I avoided repeating assembly, capture, and raw-read fields already generated elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Name of the annotation software used to assign genes and functional features to the draft genome; for this workflow it should identify the tool actually applied.
Version of the annotation software used in this process step, recorded as the exact release string executed for genome annotation.
Repository, package source, or reference location for the annotation software used in this step, such as a GitHub URL, conda package name, or published release citation.
Reference database or database set used for functional annotation, such as protein, gene, or pathway databases consulted during the annotation process.
Version or release date of the annotation database used in this process step, recorded as the exact database version accessed during annotation.
Gene prediction mode or model selection used by the annotation pipeline, if applicable; for example, prodigal mode, metagenome mode, or default annotation settings.
Minimum open reading frame length in base pairs considered during annotation, measured as the configured cutoff for gene calling or feature prediction.
Total number of predicted genes generated by the annotation process, recorded as a process-level output metric for the annotation run.
Total number of functional features assigned during annotation, such as rRNA, tRNA, CDS, or pathway-related labels, recorded as a process-level output metric.
Whether the annotation process completed successfully and produced a usable annotated genome, based on pipeline execution status. Record as a process-level outcome indicator.

annotated_sag_genome.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed annotation product itself, not the annotation software or the underlying draft genome sequence. I included fields that summarize the annotated genome as a data object: identifier, gene and feature counts, presence of common annotation classes, file/storage attributes, and a basic annotation confidence or completeness-style summary. I excluded annotation software, database, and gene-calling settings because those belong to the genome_annotation Process node, and I excluded assembly metrics and raw-read properties because those belong upstream. I also avoided repeating fields already generated for the draft genome derivative or other nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the annotated SAG genome product; use a stable string format such as SAGANN_001. This identifies the computed annotation derivative, not the draft assembly or annotation run.
Number of predicted genes represented in the annotated genome product, recorded as a property of the derivative annotation output.
Number of functional labels, product names, or other annotation assignments contained in the annotated genome product, recorded as a property of the derivative output.
Count of ribosomal RNA features annotated in the genome product, if reported. Record the number of rRNA features present in the final annotation derivative.
Count of transfer RNA features annotated in the genome product, if reported. Record the number of tRNA features present in the final annotation derivative.
GC content of the annotated genome product, expressed as a percentage of total bases represented in the annotated derivative sequence.

Optional numeric confidence or support score summarizing the annotation product quality, if the pipeline reports one. Record the score as a derivative-level summary of annotation reliability, typically on a tool-specific scale.
File format of the annotated genome output, such as GFF, GBK, GenBank, or another annotation delivery format. Record the technical file type of the derivative artifact.
File path, object store URI, or archive accession where the annotated genome product is stored; for example, a local path, cloud bucket URI, or repository accession.
Checksum or hash for the annotated genome file used to verify data integrity, such as MD5 or SHA256. Record the technical integrity identifier for the derivative artifact.

assembly_qc_metrics.reasoning: This Process node should describe how assembly quality metrics were computed from the draft genome using QC software. I included QC software identity, version, reference database or marker set, and the principal metrics calculated by the tool because those belong to the measurement/summary process. I excluded the draft genome sequence properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the final quality table file properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating assembly or annotation fields already generated elsewhere, while keeping the schema focused on reportable assembly assessment outputs.

md_schema.descr: Name of the quality-control software used to compute assembly summaries such as completeness and contamination; for this workflow it should identify the tool actually applied.
Version of the QC software used in this process step, recorded as the exact release string executed for assembly assessment.
Repository, package source, or reference location for the QC software used in this step, such as a GitHub URL, conda package name, or published release citation.
Reference database, marker set, or lineage-specific dataset used by the QC software to evaluate assembly quality; for example, single-copy marker sets used for completeness estimation.
Method used to estimate genome completeness in the QC step, such as marker-gene-based assessment or another supported approach. Record the assessment strategy applied to the draft assembly.
Estimated genome completeness reported by the QC software, expressed as a percentage at the end of the assessment. Typical values range from 0 to 100.
Estimated genome contamination reported by the QC software, expressed as a percentage at the end of the assessment. Typical values range from 0 to 100.
Name of the contiguity metric calculated by the QC step, such as N50, L50, or another assembly-contiguity summary. Record the metric explicitly reported by the software.

Numeric value of the selected contiguity metric computed for the draft assembly, measured at the end of QC. Use base pairs for N50-like metrics or unitless counts for L50-like metrics as appropriate to the chosen metric.
Whether the draft assembly met the laboratory’s or pipeline’s predefined QC criteria after metric computation. Record as a process-level outcome indicator for the QC step.

assembly_quality_table.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed assembly quality table itself, not the QC software or the draft genome. I included table identity, file characteristics, metric coverage, and storage/integrity fields because those describe the derivative artifact used for downstream comparisons. I excluded the underlying metric computation method because that belongs to the assembly_qc_metrics Process node, and I excluded raw assembly sequence properties because those belong to the draft_sag_genome Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields from earlier nodes, while keeping the schema oriented toward the reportable summary table.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the assembly quality table derivative; use a stable string format such as SAGQC_001. This identifies the computed summary table, not the QC software run.
File format of the assembly quality table, such as TSV, CSV, XLSX, or JSON. Record the technical format of the derivative table artifact.
Number of rows contained in the quality table at the time it was generated, representing the number of SAG assemblies or records summarized in the derivative file.
Number of columns or fields contained in the quality table at the time it was generated, representing the metric dimensions included in the derivative file.

Names of the assembly quality metrics included in the table, recorded as a compact string or delimited list such as completeness, contamination, N50, and total length. This describes the content of the derivative table.
File path, object store URI, or archive accession where the quality table is stored; for example, a local path, cloud bucket URI, or repository accession.
Checksum or hash for the quality table file used to verify data integrity, such as MD5 or SHA256. Record the technical integrity identifier for the derivative artifact.
Date when the assembly quality table was generated, recorded in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. This documents the derivation time point for the summary artifact.
Brief free-text note describing any notable characteristics of the quality table, such as whether it aggregates multiple SAGs or includes one table per assembly.
